# Ghost in the Machine — the questline

_JackieLives 2.0. Generated from the shipped story data (2.0-a1)._

## The story

**Dramatic question.** What did it cost to keep Jackie Welles alive — and who gets to decide
whether he pays it?

**Theme — salvage.** Everyone here is built out of parts meant for something else.

| | Wants | Needs | Flaw | Completes when |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Jackie** | To stay out, and to be enough without a gun | To accept the man who died at Konpeki isn't coming back | "I'm fine, mano" | He tells V the truth before being asked |
| **V** | To keep Jackie safe | To stop managing him | The reunion lie about the Relic | They hand him back the choice — or knowingly don't |

## Structure

| Part | Title | What it is | Rests at |
|---|---|---|---|
| P1 | **Static** | Jackie's hand stops working for four seconds, and he lies about it. That night he tells the truth in a text, because he can't say it out loud. | V and Jackie both know. Nobody else does. Nothing is chasing anybody yet. |
| P2 | **Phone Home** | The beacon in Jackie's shoulder has been talking to Arasaka for fourteen months, and somebody has finally started listening. | Jackie can walk through Night City again. The other problem just woke up. |
| P3 | **Passenger** | The thing in Jackie's operating system has spent fourteen months learning how to be him, and it is getting good at it. | The operation is funded and booked for Thursday. Jackie has come as close to saying he is frightened as his own recorded voice allows, and then said the rest of it in writing at four in the morning. |
| P4 | **Salvage** | Thursday. Vik's table. Three ways this can go and none of them gives Jackie back. | The operation is over. Which Jackie walks out of it is now a permanent property of this save, and every companion system reads it. |
| P5 | **After** | What it is like now — which is a different question in each of the three saves, and the only one the mod has left to answer. | Done. Jackie stays in the world as whichever version of himself the player left him. |

## P1 — "Static"

> Jackie's hand stops working for four seconds, and he lies about it. That night he tells the truth in a text, because he can't say it out loud.

**What this part is for.** Establish the flaw (he lies), the symptom (his body), and the private channel (SMS) in that order. The player should finish this part understanding that Jackie will always tell them less in person than in writing — which is the mechanic the whole arc is built on.

**Opens when:** the retrieval questline is finished, 3 in-game days since the reunion, familiarity at least 1.

### The first one you see — `p1_episode`

**episode** · anywhere · 06:00–00:00 · with jackie

Not a cutscene. It happens mid-follow, while the player is going somewhere else, and it is over before they have finished reacting. Four seconds. The player should not be sure what they just saw.

**On screen:**
- halt him (existing halt/workspot machinery)
- hold a gesture pose — his right hand
- cut a VO line short mid-word, 0.4s of silence, re-fire it (the audio glitch)
- short screen distortion (the existing glitch effect used at reunion)
- release; he walks on

_Voice: after: deflect_light_

_Note: If the player asks him about it (talk prompt within 30s), he uses deflect_light again, not a new line. He has nothing else to say yet._

### Ripperdoc scan — patient: J. Welles — `p1_scan`

**shard** · Vik's clinic

The reveal lands as a DOCUMENT, not a speech, for three reasons: Vik has no new VO, a scan is what a ripperdoc would actually produce, and a document stays in the Codex where the player can re-read it when Part 3 makes it matter.

**Shard — "Ripperdoc scan — patient: J. Welles"** (Viktor Vektor):

> PATIENT: Welles, J. — post-trauma review, 14 months.
> 
> Two foreign objects. Neither of them mine.
> 
> OBJECT ONE. Militech-pattern housing, Arasaka firmware. Sits in the left shoulder assembly. It's a factory anti-theft telemetry unit — mil-spec parts phone home so the company knows where its property is. It has been transmitting, on a low duty cycle, since the night I put it in him. For most of that time nobody was listening.
> 
> OBJECT TWO. Not hardware. There's a suppression daemon resident in his operating system — corp security payload, the kind a netrunner burns into you to shut your limbs off. It never finished executing. He flatlined halfway through the attack, and a dead man is a bad host, so it stalled. It has not stalled since. It has been learning his neural pattern for fourteen months.
> 
> For the record, because he won't ask and she will:
> 
> I had a dying man on my table and four hours. What I put in him is what was in the room. It came off the same job that killed him. I'd do it again — he's breathing — but nobody should pretend I did surgery that night. I did salvage.
> 
> — V.V.

### Pull it now, or find the proper fix — `p1_choice`

**choice** · Vik's clinic · with jackie, vik

A first-act turn that does NOT branch the plot — it branches the CHARACTER. Whichever way the player goes, Vik refuses to operate blind, so the story is the same story. What changes is whether Jackie spends the next four parts knowing he asked to get out early and was overruled. That colours every line he has.

**Choices:**

- **"Take it out. All of it. Now."**
  Vik: he'd survive it. He'd also be a man who gets winded on stairs. Jackie says yes anyway. Vik refuses to cut blind — he doesn't know what the daemon does if you unplug its host.
- **"We do it right. Whatever it takes."**
  Jackie is relieved and hides it badly. He has been dreading being told to give up the chrome, which tells the player something he hasn't said.
- **"It's your body, Jackie."**
  He doesn't answer. That is the answer, and it is the seed of Part 4 — the man cannot make this decision about himself.

_Voice: close: thanks_v_

## P2 — "Phone Home"

> The beacon in Jackie's shoulder has been talking to Arasaka for fourteen months, and somebody has finally started listening.

**What this part is for.** Turn the premise into a MECHANIC. Heat accrues while Jackie is out in the world with V, which means the threat is generated by the thing the player most enjoys — having him around. The quiet horror of this part is not the snatch squads. It is that Jackie is happier in the first firefight than he has been since he came home, and the player notices before he does.

**Opens when:** the arc has reached stage 1, 4 in-game days since the previous part, familiarity at least 1.

**Heat.** A hidden counter (`jackielives_trace`) that rises while Jackie is out in the world with V and
never decays on its own:

| Threshold | What happens |
|---|---|
| 25 | `p2_unknown_number` |
| 55 | `p2_drone` |
| 85 | `p2_squad` |

### Something's watching — `p2_drone`

**scene** · wherever Jackie is · 06:00–02:00

Escalation without violence. A surveillance drone holds station over wherever Jackie is idling. The player can shoot it or leave it; both are the same outcome, because it already saw him. Giving the player a meaningless choice here is deliberate — it teaches them that they cannot shoot their way out of this particular problem, one part before they try.

**On screen:**
- spawn surveillance drone at 30m altitude over Jackie's venue
- it holds for ~40s, then leaves regardless
- if destroyed: Jackie reacts (angry_corp), heat +10 anyway

### Burn it or spoof it — `p2_choice`

**choice** · with jackie, nix_remote

A real strategic fork with a long fuse. Neither option is safe; they are unsafe at different times, which is the only kind of choice worth writing.

**Choices:**

- **"Burn it. Kill the beacon."**
  The beacon dies. Heat stops accruing and resets to zero — Jackie can walk through Night City again. But a mil-spec unit going dark is itself an event, and Arasaka logs it. This is what makes Part 5's raid possible.
- **"Spoof it. Let them keep listening to a lie."**
  Nix feeds it a loop: asset in transit, catalogued, unremarkable. Heat freezes where it is and never resets. The spoof degrades. One late squad arrives no matter what the player does.

### The pulse — `p2_midpoint`

**episode** · Badlands comms mast *(coords not captured yet)*

THE MIDPOINT REVERSAL, and the single most important structural beat in the arc. The player has just solved the problem the whole part was about. Ninety seconds later, the jammer pulse — or the beacon dying, depending on the branch — reaches the other Arasaka thing inside him and wakes it up properly. The victory caused the disaster. Everything after this is downhill and it is the player's own doing.

**On screen:**
- Jackie drops mid-sentence — a full collapse, not a stumble
- eight seconds of nothing; V cannot wake him
- he comes back up on his own, doesn't know he went down
- audio glitch on the recovery line — the SAME glitch as p1_episode, longer

_Voice: after: deflect_hard, onWake: confused_

## P3 — "Passenger"

> The thing in Jackie's operating system has spent fourteen months learning how to be him, and it is getting good at it.

**What this part is for.** This is the horror part, and horror in this mod means MEDICAL, not monstrous. The escalation ladder is spread across days so the player lives with it. The takeover is the all-is-lost beat; Vik tapping out is the dark night of the soul; the gig is the false dawn that gets them to Part 4.

**Opens when:** the arc has reached stage 2, 5 in-game days since the previous part, familiarity at least 2.

### Ten minutes — `p3_blackout`

**episode** · Misty's Esoterica · 12:00–21:00 · with jackie, misty

Escalation step one. He loses ten minutes at Misty's and lies about it — and the lie is CHECKABLE, because his own texts have timestamps. This is a thing text can do that voice cannot, and it is the reason the SMS system earns its place twice in this arc.

**The texts** (thread `jackie`):

> **jackie:** at mistys. come by when you're done  
> _(14:02)_
> **jackie:** you coming or what  
> _(14:14 — twelve minutes later, and he has no memory of the first one)_

_Voice: onArrive: confused, onPressed: deflect_hard_

### The timestamps — `p3_timestamps`

**talk** · Misty's Esoterica · with jackie

THE PAYOFF OF V'S FLAW. V shows him his own phone to prove he blacked out — and he turns it round: 'You wanna talk about what people don't tell each other?' He has known since the reunion that V lied to him about the Relic. He let it go because he was grateful to be alive. He is not letting it go now.

**Choices:**

- **"You're right. I lied to you. About the Relic, about all of it."**
  The only route to the arc's warmest ending. He doesn't forgive V in the scene — he says 'okay' and changes the subject, and then texts something kind at 3am, because that is who he is.
- **"That's not what this is about."**
  He lets it drop. It comes back in Part 4 — if V never admitted the lie, Jackie will not accept V making the decision for him, and the 'you choose' ending is the only one that plays honestly.

_Voice: close: goodbye_soft, open: deflect_hard_

### Vik taps out — `p3_vik_taps_out`

**shard** · Vik's clinic

The dark night of the soul, delivered as a document because Vik saying it out loud is not something we can record. One sentence in it is the sentence the entire series exists to earn.

**Shard — "From Vik — read this alone"** (Viktor Vektor):

> I've had two days with the scan and I'm going to tell you the part I didn't tell him.
> 
> I can trap the daemon, or I can take the chrome out. I can't do both, and I can't do either alone.
> 
> Trapping it means walling it off inside the hardware it's living in. The hardware stays. So does everything it's doing to him, just slower, and he comes to see me every few weeks for the rest of his life.
> 
> Taking it out is cleaner and it's worse. That thing has been running on his neural pattern for fourteen months. It isn't sitting next to him any more. It's using his roads. Pull it and some of him comes with it — and before you ask me how much: I don't know. Nobody knows. There's no literature on this because nobody survives the part where you flatline mid-attack.
> 
> Whatever you do, he needs replacement chrome that Arasaka never touched, and that's not a favour I can do you. That's money.
> 
> One more thing, and then I'll shut up.
> 
> He asked me, when he came round the first time, whether he was still him. I told him yes because he was on my table and it was the only useful thing to say. I've been carrying that answer around for over a year now and I'd like somebody else to have a turn.
> 
> — Vik

### At one remove — `p3_afraid`

**scene** · El Coyote Cojo · with jackie

The emotional apex of the arc, and the audit rewrote it for the better. The plan was for Jackie to say he is afraid, out loud, in his own voice. The corpus does not contain the word — not 'afraid', not 'scared', not once in 1101 lines. What it contains instead is this: 'Worried 'bout me. Been for a while.' He can tell you that somebody ELSE is frightened for him. That is the whole of his range, and it is a better scene than the one that was planned, because a man whose defining flaw is that he cannot say things does not get to say the biggest one. So: he talks about Misty being worried. He does not finish the sentence. Then he asks V whether they want another beer.

_Voice: line: worried_remove, then_: deflect_light_

_Note: The actual admission arrives four hours later, in writing, in p3_ask — which is the arc's thesis expressed as a delivery mechanism. Play this beat with NO music cue and no camera work. It is two people at a bar._

## P4 — "Salvage"

> Thursday. Vik's table. Three ways this can go and none of them gives Jackie back.

**What this part is for.** One room, one choice, permanent consequences. Everything before this exists to make the player unable to pick easily. The design rule: all three endings are defensible, none is the good one, and the mod never tells the player which one it approves of — not in the text, not in the achievement, not in Jackie's face.

**Opens when:** the arc has reached stage 3.

### Last call — `p4_night_before`

**scene** · El Coyote Cojo · with jackie

The pre-battle bonding scene, which is a cliché because it works. Slot the side quest 'Last Call' here if the player hasn't played it. This is the mod's last chance to be warm and it should take it without apologising.

_Voice: close: goodbye_soft, during: misty_ref, open: lets_go_

### Vik's table — `p4_table`

**travel** · Vik's clinic · 08:00–14:00

A short walk with a long silence. The objective is trivially easy on purpose — the mod should not ask the player to be good at anything today.

**Journal objective:** Be there — Vik's clinic, Thursday morning

### The choice — `p4_choice`

**choice** · with jackie, vik

Four options, three outcomes. The fourth — handing it back — is the arc's thesis and resolves V's arc rather than Jackie's: it is V finally stopping managing him. It is not a secret good ending. It costs the player the ability to control the outcome, and the mod means that.

**Choices:**

- **"Take it all out."** → ending: Clean
  Everything Arasaka comes out, and the daemon goes with it — and so does the edge. He is ordinary now.
- **"Wall it off. Keep the chrome."** → ending: Caged
  The companion the player already knows — with upkeep. Alive, not cured.
- **"Don't cut. Walk out."** → ending: Ride it
  The strongest Jackie in the mod, on borrowed time, with Arasaka still coming. This is the ending that Part 2's firefight argued for.
- **"No. You choose, Jackie."** → ending: His call
  He is angry for about four seconds and then he goes quiet, and then he chooses — and what he chooses is read off what the player has actually taught him about himself.
  Read off the save, in order:
    - `caught_lie == 1 and familiarity >= 3` → ending 2 — V admitted the lie and he trusts them. He picks the one that keeps him here, with upkeep, because staying is worth the trouble.
    - `pull_now == 1` → ending 1 — He asked to get it all out in Part 1 and was overruled. He has not changed his mind; he was just waiting to be allowed.
    - `episodes >= 4 or knows_mama == 1` → ending 1 — He has seen what he does to the people around him. He picks safety.
    - `familiarity <= 1 or caught_lie == 2` → ending 3 — He was never let in far enough to want the quiet life. He goes back to the only thing he was ever certain he was good at.
    - otherwise → ending 2

_Note: NO LINE PLAYS HERE, and that is the audit's doing: the corpus has no farewell with any                  weight in it (see M.CASTING note 2). Jackie says nothing while Vik preps the table.                  A borrowed casual "Ahí luego" under the biggest moment in the mod would have been                  worse than silence, and silence is what a man who cannot say things does anyway._

## P5 — "After"

> What it is like now — which is a different question in each of the three saves, and the only one the mod has left to answer.

**What this part is for.** Short. Three of them, one each, and the player only ever sees theirs. An epilogue's job is not to explain the ending — it is to let the player sit in it for ten minutes and find out how they feel.

**Opens when:** the arc has reached stage 4, 2 in-game days since the previous part.

### A place at the table — `p5a_table`

**scene** · El Coyote Cojo · 19:00–22:00 · with jackie, mama

The warm one, and it is warm because it is small. Mama's dinner, the plate that has been laid every week since he 'died', and the note underneath it that says she knew — which retroactively makes every 'don't tell Mama' in the arc into something sadder and better.

**Shard — "A note, folded under a plate"** (Guadalupe Welles):

> Jaquito.

> You think I don't know my own son's hands.

> 
> I am not going to ask you what it was. You would lie, and then I would have to decide whether to let you.
> 
> Eat something. You are too thin. Bring your friend.
> 
> — Mamá

_Voice: close: thanks_v, open: mama_ref_

### Recovery in progress — `p5c_raid`

**fight** · Rocky Ridge garage · 02:00–06:00 · with jackie, arasaka_squad, rico?

The one earned set-piece in the mod. Arasaka comes to where Jackie sleeps, in force, and he goes back to Rocky Ridge — the garage where V found him in Act I — because it is the only place he ever felt safe. The mod ends where it began, which is not a coincidence and should not be explained to the player.

## The side quests

| Quest | Slot | Length | What it plants |
|---|---|---|---|
| **The Arch** | anytime | 15 min | The Arch itself. Part 5C's escape is on this bike; Part 5A is him handing the keys back for good, which is the quietest way the mod has of saying he knows what he is now. |
| **Last Rites** | before:p3 | 20 min | Part 4: 'I already got a wall, mano. Don't put me on it twice.' Do not use that line anywhere else, and do not use it at all if this quest was never played — a callback to nothing is worse than no callback. |
| **Padre's Favour** | before:p3 | 25 min | Rico. He is the kid in the room during Part 3's takeover, which is what makes that beat unbearable rather than merely alarming — and he is the one who turns up with four Valentinos in Part 5C, uninvited, because Jackie once decided not to hurt him. |
| **Mama's Errand** | anytime | 20 min | The plate. Mama lays one for Jackie every week and has since the funeral; here it reads as a running joke about her cooking too much. In Part 5A it is the payoff, and in her note it is the proof she knew all along. |
| **A Reading** | before:p4 | 10 min | Part 5. The card is on the bar in the epilogue, face up, matching the ending the player got. Nobody comments on it. If the player never played this quest there is no card, and that is fine — the epilogue does not depend on it. |
| **House Rules** | anytime | 20 min | Nothing. One quest in nine is allowed to plant nothing, and pretending otherwise is how a mod becomes homework. |
| **The Noodle Question** | anytime | 10 min | A running joke, which counts. In Part 5A he orders V's stand's food without being asked, and does not acknowledge that he has done it. |
| **Coyote's Cut** | between:p2,p3 | 25 min | Part 4's third ending, again. Two quests argue for 'Ride it'. Neither of them says so. |
| **Last Call** | arc:p4_night_before | 20 min | Nothing. It collects. |

### The Arch — `side_bike`

> V has been carrying the keys to a dead man's motorcycle for a year. He isn't dead.

The first side quest anyone should play, because it is the one that hurts in the cheapest way: nothing happens in it. There is no fight, no fixer, no eddies. There is a set of keys in V's inventory that the game gave them as a memorial, and a man standing in front of them who is not memorialised. The mod has had 'his bike' sitting in the design doc as a TODO since 2024 (DESIGN.md §10.5). This is it.

- `bike_sms` — **sms**
- `bike_handover` — **scene** · El Coyote Cojo · 20:00–02:00
  He does not take them. He looks at them on the bar for a while and says the bike was never really his either — he was still paying it off when he 'died', and somebody at the dealership has presumably written him a very confused letter. Then he takes them. Comedy first, weight second, in that order, always.
    - **"[Hand over the keys]"** 
    - **"Keep it at mine. You ride it whenever."** — He agrees far too fast. He does not want it parked outside Mama's where she has to look at it.

### Last Rites — `side_wall`

> Somebody keeps lighting candles under Jackie Welles' name.

The heaviest of the side quests and the one that earns Part 4's best line. Heywood put him on a memorial wall. The candles are still being replaced by a woman on his street who does not know and would not believe it. He goes at 3am so nobody sees him. Structurally this is a HORROR image played completely straight — a man reading his own name — and the mod should not comment on it. No music, no dialogue for the first thirty seconds. Let the player stand there.

- `wall_sms` — **sms**
- `wall_visit` — **scene** · The Heywood memorial wall *(coords not captured yet)* · 02:00–05:00
    - **"I should've told them. All of them."** — 'Nah. Would've made it worse.' He is wrong and they both know it.
    - **"Who's lighting them?"** — Señora Ruiz, four doors down, every Sunday for a year. He has been avoiding her street. This is the detail that makes the wall real.
    - **"[Say nothing]"** — The best option and the mod should not tell the player that.

### Padre's Favour — `side_rico`

> A Valentino kid owes money to people who break fingers. Jackie has been sent to break them.

The quest that proves what 'community fixer' means, by showing the job Jackie will NOT do. Padre asks him to collect; he goes, finds a nineteen-year-old, and pays the debt himself out of money he does not have. That is the character thesis of the whole mod delivered in one action instead of a paragraph — and it sets up Part 3's money problem with a reason he is broke that is entirely to his credit.

- `rico_call` — **sms**
- `rico_find` — **travel** · The Part 3 gig site *(coords not captured yet)* · 16:00–00:00
- `rico_choice` — **choice**
  V's choice, not Jackie's — because the mod should occasionally let the player be the one who decides who Jackie gets to be. If V insists on collecting, he does it, and he is quiet for two in-game days afterwards, and that is the whole punishment. No fail state, no lecture.
    - **"[Pay the kid's debt — €$2,000]"** — Jackie pays half before V can finish the sentence. He was always going to.
    - **"Scare him. Don't touch him."** — Works. Jackie hates it. Rico remembers V's face, not Jackie's.
    - **"Padre asked for fingers."** — He does it, and he doesn't argue, and he doesn't look at V for two days.

### Mama's Errand — `side_dinner`

> Nine items. One shopping list. Two grown men who cannot follow it.

Pure comedy, and the mod's warmest twenty minutes. Mama sends them for ingredients; the list is in Spanish; Jackie cannot read his mother's handwriting; they buy the wrong chillies twice. It ends at her table. Every serious mod needs one quest whose only stake is a sauce, and this is that quest — but it is also where the arc's saddest prop gets established, and the player will not notice it going in.

- `dinner_list` — **sms**
- `dinner_market` — **travel** · Redwood Market · 08:00–18:00
- `dinner_table` — **scene** · El Coyote Cojo · 19:00–22:00
  Uses the shipped dinner system. One shot matters: the extra plate at the end of the table, laid, empty, and never mentioned by anybody.

### A Reading — `side_card`

> Misty deals for Jackie. Jackie does not want to be dealt for.

Ten minutes, one card, and the mod's only supernatural gesture — kept ambiguous, because Misty's whole function in Cyberpunk is to be right in a way you can argue with. She deals him a card and reads it kindly. Which card she deals is DETERMINISTIC, picked from where the arc actually stands, so a player on a second playthrough gets a different one and feels the mod watching them.

- `card_read` — **scene** · Misty's Esoterica · 10:00–21:00
    - **"[Let her finish]"** 
    - **"It's cardboard, Misty."** — She agrees pleasantly and keeps reading. You cannot win an argument with Misty and the mod should not let the player try.

### House Rules — `side_houserules`

> Two Valentinos, one card game, and a bar Jackie is supposed to be keeping calm.

The bar-fight comedy. It escalates in exactly three steps — an argument, a shove, a table — and the joke is that Jackie's fixer voice works perfectly right up until someone insults his mother's bar, at which point he is nineteen again. Fists only; nobody dies; Mama bans everyone for a week including Jackie.

- `hr_fight` — **fight** · El Coyote Cojo · 21:00–03:00
    - **"[Talk them down]"** — Works. Jackie is visibly disappointed.
    - **"[Throw the first punch]"** — Jackie is delighted and says so for two days.

### The Noodle Question — `side_noodles`

> There are two noodle stands. Jackie has opinions. The other stand has opinions about Jackie.

The smallest quest in the mod and the one most likely to be someone's favourite. A ten-minute neighbourhood feud with no violence, no eddies and no consequence, in which V has to eat at both stands and pick one, and whichever they pick Jackie argues with. The mod remembers the answer and he brings it up for the rest of the game. That is the entire feature and it is worth building.

- `noodle_taste` — **scene** · The noodle bar · 08:00–14:00
    - **"Yours. Obviously yours."** — He does not believe V and interrogates them.
    - **"The other one. Sorry."** — Genuine betrayal. Ten minutes of it.
    - **"They're the same noodles, Jackie."** — The nuclear option. He does not speak on the walk back.

### Coyote's Cut — `side_shakedown`

> Somebody has decided Mama Welles pays protection now.

The one side quest with real violence, deliberately placed in the gap between Parts 2 and 3 — after the player has learned that Jackie enjoys fighting, before they learn what it costs. It is a straight fight in a place the player cares about, and its real function is to let them see him be good at this ONE more time while he still is.

- `cut_sms` — **sms**
- `cut_fight` — **fight** · El Coyote Cojo · 20:00–00:00

### Last Call — `side_lastcall`

> The night before the operation. The bar is closed. He has the keys.

The pre-battle drink — a cliché, used on purpose, because the reason it is a cliché is that it works. It is the mod's last warm scene and it must not be clever. No plot advances. No new information. They sit in a closed bar and Jackie tells the single worst story he has, badly, for the fourth time, and V has the option of pretending they have not heard it.  Every callback the save has earned fires here, one after another, and this is the beat where a player who played the side quests gets a visibly different scene from one who did not. That is the reward for all nine of them.

- `lastcall` — **scene** · El Coyote Cojo · 22:00–04:00
    - **"You've told me this one."** — 'I know.' He tells it anyway.
    - **"[Let him tell it]"** 
    - **"Are you scared?"** — The only time anyone in the mod asks the question directly. He says 'nah' and then sits there for eleven seconds without saying anything else, which is the answer. The dialogue widget must hold the pause — do not close the node early.
    - callback: side_wall  -> 'I already got a wall, mano. Don't put me on it twice.'
    - callback: side_bike  -> he leaves the Arch keys on the bar and does not explain
    - callback: side_rico  -> Rico is wiping down tables and will not go home
    - callback: side_card  -> Misty's card is in his jacket pocket and he pretends it isn't
    - callback: side_noodles -> he has already ordered from V's stand
    - callback: side_dinner-> Mama comes down, looks at them both, and goes back up without a word

## What still needs capturing in-game

Until each is captured the engine falls back to the place named in M.PLACES[x].fallbackKey and writes one line to the log. Nothing breaks; the scene just happens somewhere less good.

| Place | Why | How |
|---|---|---|
| `coyote_back` | Part 3's takeover | Back/storeroom area of El Coyote Cojo, facing the door. |
| `mast` | Part 2's jammer plant | A Badlands comms mast with a driveable approach — stand at its base. |
| `wall` | Side quest 'Last Rites' | A memorial wall in Heywood (Vista del Rey has several) — face it. |
| `gig_lot` | Part 3's paying job | An open industrial lot with cover, Santo Domingo, no civilians. |

## Casting — what Jackie can actually say

Every beat names a *casting slot*, never a recording. These are the slots and what the audit
(`docs/research/arc_casting.md`) found for each.

| Slot | Recordings | What it has to carry |
|---|---|---|
| `angry_corp` | 3 | Corp hate. 'I hate these 'borg fuckers.' Also carries the recognition beat — he can't say 'they came for me', so he says what he thinks of them. |
| `chrome_ref` | 1 | 'Great piece of chrome. Feels like fucking Christmas morning.' Tonally WRONG for the reveal — which is why it belongs early, before he knows. Irony is free. |
| `combat_call` | 5 | Tactical barks. Deep pool, no scarcity — the fights are the one place the library is generous. |
| `combat_joy` | 3 | He is ENJOYING this. Part 4's third ending is argued for entirely by these three lines. |
| `confused` | 1 | Disoriented. Doubles with deflect_hard on purpose — being lost and covering it are the same sound in him. |
| `deflect_hard` | 2 | The same deflection with the shutters down. 'Agh, I dunno…' / 'Agh, don't thrill you, that?' |
| `deflect_light` | 1 | The brush-off. 'Don't worry, got this.' The closest the corpus comes to 'I'm fine' — there is no better one. |
| `goodbye_soft` | 1 | The one unspent 'Ahí luego. I will.' Everything else in the farewell pool is burned by retrieval.lua. |
| `laugh` | 0 | A real laugh. UNCAST — audit found none clean; relief beats fall back to lets_go/toast. |
| `lets_go` | 3 | Movement. Unspent alternatives to the ones retrieval.lua already drains. |
| `mama_ref` | 2 | Only two exist in 1101 lines, both about her cooking — which is why Part 5A is a dinner and not a conversation. |
| `misty_ref` | 3 | 'Misty asked me… not to take this job.' Already voiced, already exactly Part 3's objection. |
| `money_talk` | 2 | 'Won't come cheap. And it'll have to be done on the sly — no trail, hard eddies only.' It reads as though it were recorded for this arc. |
| `pain_bad` | 3 | Real damage. 'Argh… I'm leakin' a little…' Used for the midpoint collapse and the takeover recovery. |
| `pain_short` | 2 | Non-verbal distress. 1638… is pure grunt with no plot hook — the workhorse of every episode. |
| `thanks_v` | 2 | The corpus has exactly TWO real V-directed gratitude lines. Budget them: 1866… anchors Part 4's aftermath, 1993… closes Part 3. Do not spend either early. |
| `toast` | 0 | A toast. UNCAST — 'Last Call' is carried by staging and V's side of the dialogue. |
| `urgent_go` | 1 | 'There's time for thinkin', time for gettin' the fuck out! Let's go!' Unspent, high-urgency — saved for the snatch squad. |
| `vik_ref` | 3 | 'First stop – ripperdoc?' Three lines total in the corpus. Part 1's objective gets the good one. |
| `watched` | 1 | 'Watch it, V. They got cams.' Uncannily on-theme for the surveillance thread. One of the luckiest finds in the audit. |
| `worried_remove` | 2 | THE arc's emotional line, and it is at one remove: 'Worried 'bout me. Been for a while.' He can name that someone ELSE is frightened for him. That is his whole range, and the arc is built around the gap. |
